dictations.preRound: Admitted today from the hospital for rehab after urosepsis; he finished IV antibiotics there. Possible pneumonia on the hospital chest X-ray, no antibiotics for it now. He takes tamsulosin. New soft systolic murmur, ask cardiology to see him. Walks 50 feet with a walker, needs one assist for transfers. Weight 58.0 kg.
dictations.encounter: Alert and oriented. Faint crackles at the left base. PT and OT five days a week, incentive spirometer, repeat chest X-ray in one week.

note:
Reason for SNF Admission

The patient is admitted for rehabilitation following urosepsis treated with intravenous antibiotics at an outside hospital. The patient has completed the antibiotic course and is transferred to skilled nursing facility for continued recovery and rehabilitation.

Medical History and Active Comorbidities

Urosepsis — treated with intravenous antibiotics at outside hospital, course completed.
Possible pneumonia — noted on hospital chest X-ray.
New systolic murmur — identified on examination, cardiology evaluation requested.
Benign prostatic hyperplasia.

Current Medications

Tamsulosin — active

Allergies

Not dictated.

Functional Status at Admission

The patient is alert and oriented. Ambulation: 50 feet with walker. Transfers: requires one assist.

Rehabilitation Goals

Physical therapy and occupational therapy five days per week. Incentive spirometer use.

Assessment of Active Medical Problems

Urosepsis: The patient completed intravenous antibiotic therapy at the outside hospital and is admitted for rehabilitation. Clinical status stable.

Possible pneumonia: Noted on hospital chest X-ray. On examination today, faint crackles are present at the left base. No antibiotics are currently prescribed.

New systolic murmur: A soft systolic murmur has been identified. Cardiology evaluation is pending.

Benign prostatic hyperplasia: The patient is on tamsulosin.

Care Plan

1. Continue tamsulosin for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
2. Obtain repeat chest X-ray in one week to reassess possible pneumonia.
3. Physical therapy and occupational therapy five days per week.
4. Incentive spirometer daily.
5. Cardiology evaluation for new systolic murmur.
